title: Can I BEAT Martin with 1 Move on 2 Boards?
summary: Tony plays Martin on two boards simultaneously (White on both) and must play the identical move (same from/to squares) on both boards each turn; Martin answers independently. If he is mated on either board or has no move legal on both boards, he loses. Positions diverge quickly; he eventually loses when Martin promotes with checkmate on one board (~13:49).
rules: Two simultaneous standard games vs Martin; player is White on both.
Each turn the player makes ONE move that is applied identically (same origin and destination squares) on both boards.
The move must be legal on both boards; if no move is legal on both, the player loses.
Martin replies independently on each board.
win_condition: Checkmate Martin on both boards (Tony lost in the video).
